transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's good to meet you too. Um, well, what brings me in... it's just this constant, unrelenting restless feeling. It's really hard to explain, but it's like I'm wound up way too tight, you know? Like a coiled spring that just won't release. And it's all the time. I just can't seem to fully settle down, no matter what I'm doing. 

I'm a retail buyer, so I have these long, drawn-out planning meetings where we're looking at seasonal trends and spreadsheets and supplier contracts, and I'm supposed to be calmly sitting there, taking it all in, but inside I'm just buzzing. I'm shifting in my chair, tapping my pen, crossing and uncrossing my legs. It's so distracting, not just for me but probably for everyone else in the room. And it's not just at work! Even when I try to do things that are supposed to be relaxing, things I actually enjoy... like, I love to paint, I really do, but I'll set up my easel and get my colors mixed, and within ten minutes I feel this urge to just get up and pace around. Or yoga! My friends swear by yoga for relaxation, so I signed up for a class, but lying there in Savasana at the end, when everyone else is practically asleep, I'm just lying there thinking about everything I need to do and feeling this physical need to move my limbs. It's exhausting, honestly, just never being able to just... be still.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things?

Worrying? Um, no, not really. I mean, sure, I have the normal stresses of life, like anyone else. If a supplier is late with a massive holiday shipment, obviously I'll be annoyed and want to fix it, but I wouldn't call it excessive worry. It's actually funny you ask that, because my friends and family—even my coworkers—they always assume I'm anxious about something. They'll see me bouncing my leg under the conference table or pacing around the breakroom while my coffee brews, and they'll say, "What's wrong? What are you so stressed about?" 

And I always have to explain to them that I'm really not worried about anything at all! It's not a mental thing, if that makes sense? Like, my brain isn't spinning with doom and gloom, and I'm not obsessing over worst-case scenarios or anything like that. I'm not lying awake at night fretting about my taxes or wondering if I offended someone at the office. It's really just... my body. My body just feels like it needs to be in motion. 

So, no, I wouldn't say I'm a worrier. I'm actually a pretty optimistic, level-headed person overall, I just can't sit still while I'm being optimistic! I know people look at me and see someone who looks like a nervous wreck because of all the tapping and shifting and getting up and down, but inside my head, I'm usually just thinking about what I'm going to make for dinner or, you know, just desperately wishing the meeting would end so I could go for a brisk walk around the building. But as for actual worry or anxiety? No, I don't really have that going on.
Have there been times when you felt unusually energized or 'up' for several days in a row?

Unusually energized? Um, no, not really. I mean, my energy is pretty much exactly the same all the time, every single day. It’s not like I have these extreme highs and lows, you know? It's just that constant, steady hum I was telling you about. 

I definitely don't wake up one Tuesday and feel like I can suddenly conquer the world and stay awake for three days straight or anything like that. I still absolutely need my sleep! Oh my gosh, if I don't get my solid seven or eight hours, I am just completely useless at the office, especially right now when we’re in the middle of spring forecasting and I have to look at a million different vendor spreadsheets. So I'm definitely sleeping normally. 

But as for feeling "up"... no, it's not a mood thing at all. I'm not walking around feeling euphoric or super powerful or anything. It's just that physical restlessness. Like, just this past weekend, my sister was visiting from out of town, and at one point she asked me if I was on some kind of caffeine bender because I was just endlessly puttering around the house. I had reorganized the entire spice rack, then I started folding three loads of laundry, and then I went out to the yard to weed the garden, all in the span of a couple of hours. She thought I was on some kind of massive energy high! But I really wasn't. I was just doing my normal weekend routine because the thought of just sitting on the couch and watching a two-hour movie with her was making my skin crawl. 

So I wasn't "up" in my head, if that makes sense? I wasn't energized like a superhero, I just physically had to keep my hands and feet busy. It's just my baseline. It’s always there, whether it's a Monday morning or a Saturday night. So, no, I don't get these specific periods of being unusually energized for days at a time. It's just my normal everyday fidgety self.
Were you this physically restless when you were a child?

Oh, absolutely. Yes, I was exactly like this as a kid. It’s funny you ask that, because my mother brings it up all the time. She always says I was her "little tornado." I mean, I vividly remember back in elementary school—second grade, specifically, with Mrs. Gable, she had this classroom with all these fun learning stations, but I just could not stay put at my desk to save my life. I was always popping out of my seat. Like, I’d drop my pencil on purpose just to have an excuse to crawl under the desk and get it, or I'd get up to sharpen my pencil three times during a single spelling test. 

And the notes sent home! Oh my gosh, my parents got so many notes from teachers. It wasn't just the getting up, either. I was so chatty. I would just talk over my classmates constantly. We'd be in those little reading circles on the rug, and if someone was reading too slowly, I would just blurt out the end of their sentence for them because I couldn't stand waiting. I remember Mrs. Gable would ask a question to the class—like, "What is the capital of our state?" or whatever—and before she even finished the word "state," my hand was shooting up, or honestly, I wouldn't even raise my hand, I would just shout the answer out. I was always rushing to answer before the teacher even finished the question. 

It drove them crazy, I’m sure. They always said I had "ants in my pants" or that I lacked discipline, but I wasn't trying to be bad! I just felt that same exact physical buzz back then that I feel now in those endless vendor meetings. I just had to be doing something, saying something, moving somehow. So, yes, it's definitely been there since I was little. It’s just who I am, I guess, but it certainly made school... well, an adventure for everyone involved!
